checks.claim: In a septic tank, solids sink to the bottom as sludge.
checks.why: Extension and health sources: heavy solids settle to the bottom and form sludge.

sources.title: Principles of Septic Systems (Mississippi State Department of Health)

checks.claim: Grease and oils float to the top of a septic tank as scum.
checks.why: Lighter greases and fats float up and form the scum layer; the outlet tee keeps it in the tank.

sources.title: What is the purpose of a septic tank baffle? (Pumper)

checks.claim: A drain field spreads the water through perforated pipes in gravel into the soil.
checks.why: Perforated pipes in gravel trenches spread the effluent, and the soil treats it.

sources.title: Ohio State Extension fact sheet AEX-743

checks.claim: A riser brings the tank's opening up to the ground so it can be pumped.
checks.why: Risers extend the buried access opening to grade so the tank is pumped without digging.

sources.title: Septic tank risers: bring your access to ground level (Septic Solutions)
